problems.prompt: Above the onset voltage, what mainly determines whether a liquid electrosprays (fine droplets) or electrospins (a continuous fiber)?
choices: The shape of the collector plate
problems.explain: Low-viscosity liquids cannot sustain a continuous jet and break into droplets (electrospray); high-viscosity polymer solutions resist breakup and instead whip into a continuous nanofiber (electrospinning).

problems.prompt: A charged droplet breaks apart (fissions) into smaller droplets once its charge exceeds the ____ limit, at which Coulomb repulsion overcomes surface tension.
problems.explain: This is the Rayleigh limit, q_R = 8π√(ε₀γR³).

problems.prompt: Why does electrospinning produce a continuous fiber instead of separate droplets?
choices: High viscosity resists the jet breaking apart, so it instead stretches and thins under a whipping/bending instability
The voltage is too low to charge the liquid
Surface tension is zero in polymer solutions
problems.explain: Viscoelastic resistance keeps the jet intact; the whipping instability stretches and thins it into a long nanofiber rather than letting it fragment into droplets.

problems.prompt: A droplet has radius R = 5 µm and surface tension γ = 72 mN/m (0.072 N/m). Using q_R = 8π√(ε₀γR³) with ε₀ = 8.854×10⁻¹² F/m, estimate q_R in coulombs (×10⁻¹²).
